root_idea.summary: A root centered on removing, stripping, or cutting something off completely, so that it disappears.
root_idea.development: From thorough extirpation and removal, the lexicon develops meanings of destruction by punishment, property made to disappear, insatiable consumption, and unlawful gain called سُحْت because it removes blessing or leaves no lasting good.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form.
Displayed under the normalized indefinite noun citation form.

senses.definition: To destroy utterly; to annihilate or wipe out by punishment.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic threat of 20:61, the Form IV imperfective refers to destruction by punishment. The passage is also transmitted with a Form I reading and may be rendered as afflicting, overwhelming, or stripping away completely; these are nuances of the same destructive construction.

senses.definition: Forbidden or disreputable gain or property; ill-gotten proceeds whose acquisition or consumption brings disgrace.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expressions involving eating or consuming سُحْت, the term denotes unlawful or foul gain and property. Context may emphasize legal unlawfulness, moral disgrace, or both.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove, strip, scrape, or peel away completely; to efface or make something disappear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of removing the prepuce or hair, peeling fat or another thing away, and effacing traces from the surface of the earth; the construction can also describe making property disappear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slaughter or put to death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended use is attested of slaughtering people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For one's property to go away or be lost.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person's property becoming absent or disappearing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gain or earn unlawful or foul proceeds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of earning سُحْت; of trade or business, the related construction can mean that it becomes disapproved, foul, or unlawful.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To earn little or have scant returns.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested especially in descriptions of poor returns from trade.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vehemence or voraciousness in eating and drinking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun describing excessive force or greed in consumption.
A separately attested noun use in general Classical Arabic.
Used in the expression بَرْدٌ سَحْتٌ for severe cold.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bribe given to a judge or a similar authority.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional application of the noun to a corrupt or disreputable payment; related earnings may be condemned for damaging honor even where the issue is not described as strictly unlawful.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Little or small in quantity or number; paltry or inconsiderable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Classical adjective-like use describing scant amount or value.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Property that may be taken or destroyed with impunity; blood that may be shed with impunity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used idiomatically of property or blood regarded as legally or customarily open to seizure, destruction, or shedding without penalty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An old, worn-out garment or piece of cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicalized noun for a worn textile or garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A preparation of parched-grain meal with little grease or gravy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a poor or dry preparation of سَوِيق.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A desert whose earth is soft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as a description of a soft-soiled desert tract.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cloud that sweeps away what it passes over.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive use of the feminine form for a sweeping or eroding cloud.
Used of a year or a land in which there is no grazing or pasture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Property made to disappear, exhausted, or destroyed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial description of property that has been removed or made away with.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Voracious or insatiable in eating and drinking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In مَسْحُوتُ الجَوْفِ or مَسْحُوتُ المَعِدَةِ, it describes one who is not satiated or has a greedy stomach; related usage includes much eating and drinking and digestive distress.
